label: Connect rational agency and intellectual origination to the God and Catholicism case
summary: Completed a source-based comparison of two candidate contributions from philosophy of mind. Route A proposes a purposive explanation of the coordinated existence of rational embodied agents, intelligible order and effective agency; it can grant physical realization and requires an actual comparison with impersonal mind-inclusive and teleological accounts. Existing content, basing and agency results are reused, not treated as proofs that only a personal source is possible. Swinburne supplies a local motive-based comparison, with his wider divine-attribute and probabilistic commitments excluded. Route B applies Aquinas q76 ownership to q75 intellectual subsistence, q90/q118 origination, and the distinct q45 restriction on secondary creators. Weak non-inherence does not supply that full premise bundle; the existing bodily-interference rival remains decisive. The analysis favors Route A as a research priority for identifying intellect and will, with Route B complementary. It establishes no necessary intellect or Catholic conclusion. Catholic embodiment, soul creation and immortality identify relevant doctrinal targets; revelation, resurrection and Church identity retain separate evidential obligations. Full positive arguments, sources, rivals, exact bridges and next tests are in docs/notes/mind-physicalism-fork-419.md#further-contribution-to-theism-and-catholicism-2026-11-19. No theorem, registered source claim, changed statement meaning, premise closure or verified new root edge is claimed.
